description: Test your knowledge of PA H9 | Spleen Disorders.

cards.text: What is the normal weight of an adult spleen, and what are the percentages of red and white pulp?
cards.answer: Normal spleen weight is 150–200 g. Red pulp comprises ~75% (sinuses and cords of Billroth), while white pulp comprises ~25% (lymphoid tissue around PALS).

tip.tip: Remember: Red pulp is 75% (bulk of the spleen), white pulp is 25% (immune function).

cards.text: Define splenomegaly both clinically and pathologically.
cards.answer: Clinically: a palpable spleen extending below the left costal margin. Pathologically: spleen weight >250 g.

tip.tip: Clinical = palpable; Pathological = >250 g (note: normal is 150–200 g).

cards.text: What is the threshold weight and anatomical extent for massive splenomegaly?
cards.answer: Massive splenomegaly: weight >1 kg, extending to or beyond the umbilicus, or reaching the right iliac fossa (typically 3–5 kg).

tip.tip: Massive = umbilicus or beyond. Think: massive spleen reaches across the midline.

cards.text: Name the five mechanistic categories of splenomegaly.
cards.answer: 1) Congestive (raised venous pressure), 2) Infective/Inflammatory (white pulp hyperplasia), 3) Haematological (haemolytic stress or malignant infiltration), 4) Infiltrative/Storage (metabolic accumulation), 5) Immune (autoimmune activation).

tip.tip: Remember: C-I-H-I-I. Each mechanism exaggerates a normal spleen function.

cards.text: What are littoral cells, and what is their primary function?
cards.answer: Littoral cells are specialised macrophages lining the sinuses of the red pulp. They perform filtration and culling of aged, rigid, or abnormal RBCs through 3-µm slit pores.

tip.tip: Littoral cells = splenic 'bouncers' — they check RBCs and remove defective ones.

cards.text: What is the most common cause of splenomegaly in India?
cards.answer: Hepatic cirrhosis (congestive splenomegaly due to portal hypertension). Non-cirrhotic portal fibrosis (NCPF) is also common in India and causes massive splenomegaly.

tip.tip: India = Cirrhosis + NCPF. Both are congestive mechanisms (portal hypertension).

cards.text: List three causes of congestive splenomegaly and the mechanism behind each.
cards.answer: 1) Cirrhosis — intrahepatic block, 2) Portal vein thrombosis — extra-hepatic block, 3) Budd-Chiari syndrome — post-hepatic block. All raise splenic venous pressure.

tip.tip: Congestive = pressure problem. Think: pre-hepatic, intra-hepatic, post-hepatic blocks.

cards.text: What is the spleen's platelet reservoir function, and how much of total platelets are stored there?
cards.answer: The spleen stores approximately 1/3 of total circulating platelets, acting as a platelet reservoir. In splenic enlargement, platelet sequestration contributes to thrombocytopenia.

tip.tip: Splenic reserve = 1/3 of platelets. Big spleen = trapped platelets = low count.
